notes: nanobot (HKUDS/nanobot) publishes no Docker image of its own: upstream's Docker guide builds one from the repository, and it calls third-party Docker Hub images unverified. This recipe runs the official python:3.12.15-slim-bookworm image and installs the pinned PyPI release nanobot-ai==0.3.5 (the release the panel was tested with) on the first start. The wheel bundles the WebUI, so nothing is built on the server.

The install goes into its own volume (/home/nanobot/.venv) as the nanobot user. A marker file records the package and Python version; later starts skip pip, and a recipe that pins a different version (or a different Python) wipes that volume and installs again. The first start downloads about 370 MB from PyPI, so the first install takes a few minutes. Deleting the venv volume only forces a reinstall; the data volume is untouched.
Sign in with the generated web token: the WebUI opens on an Authentication required page and nothing (WebUI bootstrap, REST API or WebSocket) answers without it.
No model provider ships with the recipe. Add one in the WebUI under Settings, Models (API key and model); until then the gateway runs and replies that no provider is configured.

config.json follows upstream's Render blueprint (render-config.json at v0.3.5) and is written on the first start only, so settings saved in the WebUI survive restarts. On every start the panel re-asserts just the keys it owns: gateway host 127.0.0.1 and port 18790 (the unauthenticated health endpoint stays inside the container, as in the blueprint), and the WebSocket channel on 0.0.0.0:8765 with websocketRequiresToken, tokenIssueSecret ${NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN} (resolved by nanobot from the environment, so the token never sits in the file) and publicWsUrl wss://<domain>/ derived from NANOBOT_PUBLIC_URL. NANOBOT_PUBLIC_URL is the url key, so a domain change re-renders it and the next start updates publicWsUrl.

The blueprint's tools defaults are written on the first start: restrictToWorkspace on, webuiAllowRemotePackageInstall off and my.allowSet off. They can be changed in the WebUI afterwards; the panel does not reset them.

The agent can run shell commands, but only inside its own container, which is the boundary: no docker.sock, no extra capabilities and no host mounts. The container starts as root only to create the nanobot user (uid 1000) and hand both volumes to it; pip, the config write and the gateway all run as nanobot via setpriv, as upstream's entrypoint does. A root docker exec (the Command-line access card) is fine, and every start re-owns anything root left in the volumes.
